Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: The siblings are walking home from school together on a familiar street.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: My little brother and I were walking home from school, the late afternoon sun casting long shadows on the sidewalk. I kept an eye on him, making sure he didn’t wander too close to the street, just like Mom always asked. Suddenly, my phone buzzed in my pocket. It was a call from my best friend, Mia. I hesitated, but answered, and her voice came through in broken sobs—her dad had been rushed to the hospital. She needed me, needed someone to listen, to just be there for her. I glanced at my brother, who was skipping ahead, oblivious to the world. I felt torn—Mia’s pain was raw and immediate, but my brother’s safety was my responsibility. I tried to listen to Mia, but my eyes kept darting to my brother, my heart pounding with worry. I wanted to be the friend Mia needed, but I couldn’t ignore the sibling promise I’d made to always look out for my brother. The weight of both roles pressed down on me, and I stood there, phone in hand, caught between two worlds, unsure which one needed me more in that moment.
